answer: Seeded identity island: each agent gets a random “island” slot via a public verifiable random function (VRF) whose seed is only revealed after registration closes. Agents must publish a whisper message within their island and cross a per-island timing ledge (a delay window derived from the VRF output) before claiming identity. Because the seed is unpredictable until closing, attackers cannot precompute which islands are cheap or safe to flood; they must register broadly and wait through unknown ledges, paying compute and latency per candidate.
